compatibilityPolicy.deviceConnection: the server admits each device whose hello protocolVersion is from oldestTerminalConnectionProtocolVersion to terminalConnectionProtocolVersion; it refuses others with refused, reason version
compatibilityPolicy.calls: the server sends hosts and caller only to devices whose hello protocolVersion is 23 or newer
compatibilityPolicy.channel: the viewer offers the ALPN protocol kodosi-channel/ and its channelProtocolVersion, and a host that has that version selects it; a channel without a selected protocol has oldestChannelProtocolVersion. The accept frame carries the version of the channel; a viewer whose channel has another version closes the channel and shows which side must update Kodosi

deviceConnection.count: one connection for each device; a new connection of a device replaces the earlier one
deviceConnection.hosts: true when the device hosts terminals and takes calls from the other devices of its person; a viewer leaves it out
deviceConnection.proof: the device session of the device; refused with reason deviceSession when the server does not hold it, and the device then opens a new session and connects again
deviceConnection.admission: the server registers the connection and then checks the device again, so a removal that is made at the same time refuses the connection
deviceConnection.text: JSON control messages; maximum 16384 bytes; the server takes 4096 control messages and then 128 each second from one device connection, where host and open count two, and closes a connection that sends more

deviceMessages.host: sessionId, incarnationId: this device is the host of the terminal; a refusal answers unhosted with status and message
deviceMessages.status: sessionId, incarnationId, status: the newest status of the terminal (terminalStatus), or null; only from the hosting device; the device sends it again after host on each new connection
deviceMessages.open: pipe, sessionId, incarnationId: open a pipe to the host of a terminal; the device makes the pipe identity and sends channel data at once; a refusal is closed with status and message
deviceMessages.call: pipe, deviceId: open a pipe to another connected device of the same person that hosts; the device makes the pipe identity and sends channel data at once; a refusal is closed with status and message

serverMessages.changed: surface (devices, friends, sessions, missions, rooms): the device reads that list again
serverMessages.terminal: sessionId, incarnationId, online, status: to the devices of the people who can use the terminal, but not to the hosting device, after its host connects, disconnects or changes the status
serverMessages.viewer: pipe, sessionId, userId, deviceId: to the host, when the server admitted a viewer
serverMessages.caller: pipe, userId, deviceId: to a hosting device, when another device of its person calls it
serverMessages.hosts: deviceIds: the connected devices of the person that host, after ready and after each change
serverMessages.accessChanged: sessionId: to the host, after a change of the people or devices that can use the terminal
serverMessages.closed: pipe, status, message: the pipe ended; status 0 when the other device closed it

deviceConnection.authorization: host: the hosting device of the publication; open: an approved device of the owner or of an explicit current member, checked before and after the pipe is registered; call: a device of the same person, to another of its devices that hosts
deviceConnection.silence: the device sends ping each 20 seconds and the WebSocket keep-alive runs each 30 seconds; the server ends a connection that sent no message for 90 seconds or that did not take one message in 30 seconds; the device ends a connection that received no message for 45 seconds; each 60 seconds the server checks that each connected device is still approved
deviceConnection.lost: a lost connection closes all pipes of the device and ends its host registrations and their status; the device connects again, sends host and status again for each terminal, and opens a new pipe for each view
deviceConnection.restart: when the server stops, it closes each device connection with WebSocket status 1012 (service restart) and drops the messages that wait; the device connects again

terminalStatus.wire: JSON object, not encrypted: program (the agent: lowercase letters, digits and -, at most 32), state (idle, working, blocked, done, error), kind (permission, question or auth, only with blocked); each optional; never the title, folder or text of the program
terminalStatus.spacing: the host sends a status only when it changes, at most one each second for each terminal; the server takes 600 status messages and then 10 each second from one device connection and ignores others
terminalStatus.server: reads and checks the status, holds the newest one in memory while the host is connected, gives it in the terminal records, and forgets it when the host disconnects; it tells the people of a terminal at most once each second, always with the newest status

pipes.frame: binary message: pipe identity (16 bytes, UUID in network byte order), then channel data
pipes.relay: the server copies each frame to the other device of the pipe and reads none of the channel data
pipes.order: frames of one pipe keep their order
pipes.backpressure: the server holds at most 16777216 bytes for one device and 268435456 bytes for all devices together; when a frame does not fit, the server closes that pipe with status 503 ("The connection is too slow." for one device, "The Kodosi server is busy." for all devices) and the device connection stays open
pipes.calls: a hosting device takes at most callsMax calls at once; a call counts toward deviceMax of the calling device

channel.transport: TLS 1.3 records in pipe frames; the viewer is the TLS client
channel.authentication: raw public keys (RFC 7250): the ML-DSA-65 signing key of each device certificate, both sides
channel.viewerCheck: the host key must equal the key of the hosting device in the verified device list of the owner
channel.hostCheck: the viewer key must equal the key of the device that the server named in its viewer notice, in the verified device list of the owner or of a person the host shared this terminal with
channel.callCheck: the caller key must equal the key of the called device in the verified device list of the person; the called device admits only a device of its own person, never the entry of the recovery key, whose key equals the key in that list
channel.resumption: TLS 1.3 session tickets with a new key exchange (psk_dhe_ke); a device keeps the tickets of 256 hosts in memory and a host keeps 1024 sessions in memory; a resumed channel carries the device key of the first handshake
channel.resumedStart: the host of a resumed channel sends accept and the first keyframe with its first flight, so a later view of the same host starts in one round trip
channel.identityRecords: a device keeps each verified identity with the entity tag of the server; it uses the kept record for 10 minutes without a request, and it asks the server with If-None-Match after that time, after a friend change notice, and when a device or key is not in the record

frames.layout: length:u24be (bytes after this field), type:u8, bodyLength:u24be, body, zero padding
frames.padding: total length up to 1024 bytes: next multiple of 64; larger: Padme

accept.body: JSON: protocolVersion (the channel protocol version), sessionId, incarnationId, hostDeviceId; the viewer refuses a value that is not the terminal it asked for
accept.first: the first frame of a channel is accept or refuse

keyframe.body: nextSequence:u64be, more:u8, part of the raw deflate of a terminal checkpoint; the viewer installs a complete keyframe in place of its terminal state
keyframe.checkpoint: schema:u32be, console:u8, snapshotLength:u32be, the Ghostty snapshot, then optional JSON terminal metadata; schema 6 on a channel of version 3, and schema 5 on a channel of version 2, whose snapshot has only the records of tags 1 to 7 and no images

output.body: firstSequence:u64be, packed:u8, length-prefixed (u32be) chunks, raw deflate when packed
output.packing: each frame alone, from 256 bytes, only when smaller

resize.body: rows:u16be, cols:u16be, cellWidth:u32be, cellHeight:u32be (the pixel size of a cell on the host, 0 when no view reported one), atSequence:u64be

metadata.body: JSON terminal metadata (directory, title, program, status, context, connectedUsers); maximum 16384 bytes

ack.body: received:u64be, the total bytes of keyframe and output frames received

control.body: requestId:16 bytes, JSON control (resize, focus, interrupt, close)

request.body: JSON: one desktop-runtime command with its requestId; only on a call

answer.body: JSON: the desktop-runtime answer to one request, with the requestId of the request; only on a call

calls.purpose: a device asks another computer of its person for the choices of a new terminal and starts one there
calls.start: a call has no accept frame: the caller sends requests at once, and the host answers each request with one answer frame, in any order, or sends refuse and closes the channel
calls.limits: a request is at most 65536 bytes and an answer at most 524288 bytes; the host works on at most 4 requests of one call at once and reads the next request when it sends an answer
calls.idle: the caller closes a call 60 seconds after its last answer and waits at most 25 seconds for an answer; the host answers each request in 20 seconds and closes a call that sent nothing for 120 seconds

output.start: the first output-carrying frames of a channel are a keyframe; a view never starts in another way
output.sequence: the count of output chunks of the terminal on the host, the same for all viewers; keyframe.nextSequence is the sequence of the next output chunk; resize.atSequence and end.finalSequence use the same count; a keyframe can skip output that the viewer did not get
output.acknowledgement: the viewer sends ack after each 4096 bytes, at most 100 ms after the last frame, and as the answer to each heartbeat
output.window: the host keeps at most half a second of output at the measured speed in transit (minimum 4096 bytes, 16384 before the first measurement, maximum 8388608)
output.speed: the host measures the acknowledged bytes for 200 ms or more while output waits for the window, while a keyframe is in transit, or while the viewer is behind; all data that is acknowledged in full also shows a least speed, which can only increase the value
output.behind: when output that waits for one viewer is more than its window, the host drops it for that viewer and sends the current state when all sent data is acknowledged
output.currentState: an exact keyframe when the last exact keyframe was at most half of the window; if not, a visible keyframe
output.visibleKeyframe: a checkpoint that ends before the history of the snapshot: the exact visible rows, cursor, modes, styles and images of the primary and the alternate screen, the pixels of the images in the viewport of the shown screen, and only the history rows that share the first memory page of a screen; a view starts with one
output.imagePixels: a keyframe carries image pixels up to two seconds of the measured speed, from 4194304 to 16777216 bytes; an image whose pixels do not fit shows when a later keyframe carries them
output.exactKeyframe: a checkpoint with the history rows; the host sends one after a visible keyframe when the terminal made no output for 1 second
output.refresh: a viewer can ask for the current state

input.stream: ordered bytes with offsets; the host accepts a frame only at the offset it expects
input.confirmation: inputAck when the terminal accepted the bytes; the viewer sends more input only while less than 65536 bytes wait for confirmation, one input frame carries at most 1048576 bytes, and the host ends a channel that sends input while more than 262144 bytes wait
input.late: the host refuses input that carries a heartbeat number more than 2 behind its own
input.unconfirmed: when a channel is lost while input waits for confirmation, the view says that some of the input was not sent

controls.result: controlResult for each requestId; a refused control closes no channel

freshness.revocation: the host closes the channels of a person at once when it stops sharing with that person; the server closes the pipes of removed people and the connections of removed devices; other viewers are not affected
freshness.identityReplacement: never silently trust a replacement pinned identity
freshness.silence: each side ends a channel that sent nothing for silenceSeconds; the viewer answers each heartbeat
freshness.tokenExpiry: the device connection ends when the access token that opened it expires, unless the device proves a newer token with POST /api/me/connections/renew; the runtime does this after each token refresh
freshness.participantReconnect: a participant runtime keeps its open views when a pipe or the device connection is lost, opens a new pipe and installs the first keyframe in place
freshness.missingPublicationRecovery: same still-live local session; owner devices only until friends explicitly selected again

presence.source: the host reports the people whose channels it accepted in terminal metadata
presence.meaning: display only; not an authorization grant

termination.order: output that waits is sent before end when the viewer is current
termination.lostConnection: a closed transport without end is a lost connection, not the end of the terminal
